value_unit: provider-scoped rate-limit memory shared across distinct mutation actions
separability: standalone coordination invariant
decision_rationale: The earlier LumiNet convergence remembered 429 cooldown by action. Final cross-wave comparison shows provider quotas can span several mutation endpoints, so action-only memory still permits cross-action quota hammering. LumiNet independently generalizes the AGPL evidence into an explicit secret-free RateLimitScope shared only by mutations that declare a common provider quota boundary.
invariant: provider throttling learned by one declared action suppresses other actions in the same provider scope without globally suppressing unrelated providers
negative_invariant: scope keys must never contain URLs, credentials or request payloads, and scope sharing must never relax per-action retry safety class
migration_impact: additive policy field; undeclared callers preserve action-scoped behavior
license_note: AGPL evidence only; independently rederived; no donor code copied

value_unit: bounded per-provider mutation concurrency with fail-closed coordinator capacity
separability: standalone coordination bound
decision_rationale: The donor constrains outbound request concurrency at its provider HTTP client. LumiNet needs the stronger cross-call mutation invariant at the retry coordinator itself: declared provider scopes have a bounded in-flight gate and the coordinator refuses to allocate unbounded scope state before mutation I/O.
invariant: at most the declared bounded number of mutations may be in flight in one provider scope and coordinator scope cardinality is bounded
negative_invariant: capacity exhaustion must fail before emitting a mutation; waiting callers must remain cancellable; bounds must not coalesce semantically different mutations
migration_impact: additive bounded coordination; default in-flight limit for existing policies
license_note: AGPL evidence only; independently rederived; no donor code copied

value_unit: de-synchronized local retry backoff while preserving authoritative Retry-After
separability: standalone retry timing invariant
decision_rationale: Deterministic exponential sleeps can synchronize callers after a shared outage. LumiNet adds equal jitter only to locally chosen exponential backoff while treating provider Retry-After as authoritative and exact; this avoids herd re-entry without second-guessing provider recovery instructions.
invariant: local retry delay is randomized within a bounded interval while explicit provider delay is not jittered
negative_invariant: jitter must never extend beyond configured maximum or alter Retry-After semantics
migration_impact: timing-only hardening within existing bounded retry contract
license_note: AGPL donor behavior used as negative evidence; no donor code copied

value_unit: optimistic conditional mutation promoted from dormant compatibility manager into the canonical config owner and HTTP routes
separability: standalone stale-writer prevention contract
decision_rationale: Ninth-order implemented Caddy-like conditional mutation inside a dormant compatibility ConfigManager. The final pass promotes the invariant into LumiNet foundation/config.Manager, the actual durable settings authority, and a shared API adapter used by settings, DDNS and proxy-directory mutations. Caddy remains evidence; the live owner is no longer donor-shaped.
invariant: a stale configuration editor cannot overwrite a newer durable generation and all live HTTP config mutation routes commit through the same authority
negative_invariant: UI/body state is never authority; stale validators cannot be accepted; route-specific handlers cannot bypass the canonical config Manager
migration_impact: legacy clients without If-Match remain supported using snapshot revision; new clients can provide strong conditional mutation
license_note: Apache-2.0 mechanism adapted target-native

value_unit: restart-safe durable configuration generation preventing validator ABA
separability: standalone persistence invariant
decision_rationale: Caddy demonstrates that configuration validators must identify the active representation. A process-local counter would reset on restart and permit ABA acceptance of an old cfg-1. LumiNet therefore persists a monotonic config generation, migrates legacy files, and advances externally edited files that reuse an old generation.
invariant: the committed generation survives restart and never rolls backward for the canonical config
negative_invariant: legacy migration or external edits must not permit reuse of a previously authoritative stale validator
migration_impact: legacy config files gain _revision on first authoritative load; generation is internal metadata
license_note: Apache-2.0 test oracle; implementation is target-native durable generation rather than donor hash representation

value_unit: copy-on-write secret references composed transactionally with config publication
separability: inseparable from canonical config commit boundary
decision_rationale: Once live config mutation became transactional, the final pass found a target-local cross-store hole: overwriting a referenced secret before the config file commit could make the old file resolve to a new secret after a failed save. LumiNet stages changed secrets under new references, rolls them back on failed config commit, publishes the config, then best-effort retires superseded refs.
invariant: a failed config commit cannot mutate the meaning of the previously committed secret reference; successful publication owns the new refs before old refs are retired
negative_invariant: no currently referenced secret may be overwritten pre-commit and cleanup failure after commit must not make committed config unavailable
migration_impact: secret updates allocate a fresh native reference; obsolete refs retired after durable commit
license_note: transaction principle is permissive donor evidence; secret implementation is independent LumiNet design

value_unit: load-shed DNS responses when server write/concurrency budget is exhausted
separability: context-dependent UDP server primitive
decision_rationale: CoreDNS shed is a strong UDP-specific fail-fast primitive, but LumiNet current DNS paths already bound callers with per-client RateLimiter, PendingRequests duplicate suppression and DoH refresh coalescing/cache bounds. Importing a second shed owner would duplicate admission semantics without evidence of an uncovered fdMutex-style bottleneck in the current path.
target_capability: bounded DNS admission and duplicate suppression
invariant: DNS work remains bounded at the current target admission/coalescing owners
negative_invariant: do not add an overlapping shed controller without a measured uncovered resource bottleneck
license_note: Apache-2.0; retained as reference evidence because current target owners are stronger fit

value_unit: deduplication queue examined as a mutation-coalescing candidate and converted into a payload-identity guardrail
separability: standalone semantic constraint
decision_rationale: A unique queue is useful when element identity truly defines equivalent work. Remote mutations cannot be safely coalesced merely because they share an action or provider scope: two calls may carry different payloads. LumiNet therefore shares cooldown/capacity only; replay/coalescing remains governed by explicit idempotency and reconciliation semantics.
invariant: provider-scope coordination controls timing/capacity but never asserts payload equivalence
negative_invariant: never deduplicate arbitrary mutations by action name, provider scope or endpoint alone
license_note: no explicit license; no direct source reuse; concepts/negative evidence/reference only

value_unit: broad Unix firewall/DNS-leak rules reviewed as a target-native transaction precondition rather than imported authority
separability: standalone authority-boundary constraint
decision_rationale: InviZible and Firewalla demonstrate substantial Unix firewall/DNS-leak policy surfaces, but directly importing iptables machinery would create a second privileged host-network authority outside LumiNet’s durable snapshot/apply/verify/recover/rollback transaction. The final convergence therefore keeps Unix DNS-leak protection truthfully unsupported until it can be modeled as a first-class HostNetworkChange with reversible state capture and verification.
invariant: privileged Unix firewall mutation may become supported only through the canonical host-network transaction with durable snapshot, verification, recovery and rollback
negative_invariant: never advertise Unix DNS-leak protection or execute peer iptables rules through an untracked side authority
operator_surface: platform capability truth / DNS leak protection status
migration_impact: none; preserves truthful unsupported behavior pending a transactionally reversible implementation
license_note: GPL donor evidence only; no source copied; constraint independently derived

value_unit: unchecked endpoints stay outside active pool
separability: standalone semantic contribution
decision_rationale: The donor pool requires a measured positive latency before membership. LumiNet planner incorrectly dispatched zero-observation endpoints; the target-native fix requires at least one successful observation.
invariant: dispatch eligibility requires actual successful evidence; unknown and failed-only endpoints remain visible but inactive
negative_invariant: never infer dispatch authority from an unobserved endpoint
license_note: no explicit repository license; no direct source reuse, idea/guardrail only

separability: standalone semantic contribution
decision_rationale: The donor backs off relay failures. LumiNet polling relays previously retried failed empty polls every ticker interval. The target-native shared relay state now applies cancellation-aware capped exponential failure backoff and resets on success.
invariant: repeated upstream failure backs off in one shared relay owner and successful communication resets debt
negative_invariant: a failed relay must not be hammered at the steady-state poll cadence
license_note: no explicit repository license; no direct source reuse, idea/guardrail only

value_unit: DoH failure falls back to system DNS
separability: standalone semantic contribution
decision_rationale: Donor fallback can leak names to system DNS after privacy-path failure. LumiNet already fails closed for malformed/privacy-proxied encrypted DNS and keeps that stronger behavior.
invariant: privacy-selected encrypted DNS never silently downgrades to system DNS because its proxy path failed
negative_invariant: no privacy-mode direct/system fallback
license_note: no explicit repository license; no direct source reuse, idea/guardrail only

value_unit: local CA MITM and generated leaf certificates
separability: standalone semantic contribution
decision_rationale: Installing/generated MITM trust would enlarge LumiNet authority and contradict its strict PKI-or-explicit-pin transport model.
invariant: PKI verification is default; explicit pinning is narrow and never silently replaced by local interception
negative_invariant: do not create/install a CA or forge destination certificates for ordinary client transport
license_note: no explicit repository license; no direct source reuse, idea/guardrail only

value_unit: TLS fragmentation and out-of-band packet variants
separability: standalone semantic contribution
decision_rationale: LumiNet already owns fragmentation/evasion in its established proxy/evasion plane; donor packaging would duplicate authority and has no explicit license.
invariant: one evasion configuration owner composes supported transport variations
negative_invariant: no donor-specific second evasion runtime
license_note: no explicit repository license; no direct source reuse, idea/guardrail only

separability: standalone semantic contribution
decision_rationale: Existing runtimecore and process supervisor provide target-native lifecycle ownership and rollback; another process manager would split authority.
invariant: one lifecycle authority owns start/replace/restore/stop
negative_invariant: no donor-specific process manager authority
license_note: no explicit repository license; no direct source reuse, idea/guardrail only

value_unit: two-stage quick scan plus repeated deep qualification
separability: standalone semantic contribution
decision_rationale: Two-stage qualification is sound, but LumiNet already uses bounded repeated handshake/quality sampling with loss, median RTT, jitter and strict concurrency/candidate caps.
invariant: quality decisions use bounded repeated evidence rather than one ping
negative_invariant: scanner must not use insecure TLS or unbounded worker fanout

separability: standalone semantic contribution
decision_rationale: Scanner reachability evidence must not become transport trust. LumiNet records TLS evidence separately and keeps live transports verified.
invariant: diagnostic probing may record evidence but may not grant live transport authority
negative_invariant: no InsecureSkipVerify in user-traffic paths
license_note: MIT/permissive; direct adaptation allowed with attribution when selected

separability: standalone semantic contribution
decision_rationale: A single ping is weaker than LumiNet loss-aware multi-sample median/jitter scoring and can select flaky endpoints.
invariant: selection evidence preserves loss and distribution shape
negative_invariant: never promote one lucky ping over repeated quality evidence
license_note: MIT/permissive; direct adaptation allowed with attribution when selected

value_unit: round-robin per-stream shaper with per-stream priority heap
separability: standalone semantic contribution
decision_rationale: Fair per-stream scheduling is valuable and may improve KCP multiplexing, but replacing xtaci/smux with a fork requires protocol-compatibility and measured differential evidence. No dependency swap is justified in this pass.
invariant: a future mux replacement must prove compatibility, fairness, memory bounds and throughput under the same workload
negative_invariant: do not swap a central mux dependency from static code preference alone
license_note: MIT/permissive; direct adaptation allowed with attribution when selected

value_unit: validated frame/session/stream receive buffers and keepalive deadlines
separability: standalone semantic contribution
decision_rationale: The donor makes bounds explicit. LumiNet currently relies on the pinned xtaci/smux implementation/defaults; a future upgrade must verify equivalent bounds rather than copying fork internals.
invariant: multiplexed sessions remain bounded and keepalive timeouts are coherent
negative_invariant: no unbounded per-stream buffering
license_note: MIT/permissive; direct adaptation allowed with attribution when selected

value_unit: stateless retry and explicit connection limit
separability: standalone semantic contribution
decision_rationale: Useful QUIC server admission semantics, but qtun is a separate TCP-over-QUIC server role; LumiNet does not need another server authority.
invariant: new inbound QUIC authority requires explicit admission/resource limits
negative_invariant: do not create a second relay/server role solely to mirror donor capabilities
license_note: Cargo metadata declares MIT

value_unit: SCM_RIGHTS socket protect with 3s read/write timeouts
separability: standalone semantic contribution

invariant: one platform owner decides VPN socket protection
negative_invariant: no second JNI/Unix protect authority
license_note: Cargo metadata declares MIT

value_unit: Tor bootstrap/control events and transfer/circuit measurement schema

decision_rationale: OnionPerf provides mature measurement vocabulary (bootstrap, transfer error, circuit path/build timing) that is valuable for future Tor diagnostics, but it is a measurement framework rather than a runtime owner.

separability: standalone decision unit
decision_rationale: Shows that browser geolocation is an application-layer identity surface distinct from VPN exit IP. LumiNet keeps that distinction explicit rather than claiming VPN geolocation spoofing.
invariant: network egress identity and browser geolocation are separate authorities
negative_invariant: network routing must not be represented as browser geolocation authority
license_note: MIT

separability: standalone decision unit
decision_rationale: Timezone consistency is useful privacy-model evidence but is not a network transport responsibility.
invariant: timezone presentation belongs to browser/application identity
negative_invariant: VPN routing must not silently mutate application timezone semantics
license_note: MIT

separability: standalone decision unit
decision_rationale: WebRTC can expose network-adjacent identity outside ordinary proxy paths; retained as a diagnostic/privacy caveat.
invariant: proxy coverage claims distinguish browser peer-connection behavior
negative_invariant: transport success must not imply WebRTC identity protection
license_note: MIT

value_unit: propagate identity overrides into nested frames
separability: standalone decision unit
decision_rationale: Cross-frame propagation illustrates completeness requirements for a browser extension, but LumiNet has no browser extension authority.
invariant: browser identity overrides require child-context coverage if ever implemented
negative_invariant: partial browser overrides must not be marketed as global identity
license_note: MIT

separability: standalone decision unit
decision_rationale: Worker propagation is retained as completeness evidence only.
invariant: worker execution contexts are separate identity surfaces
negative_invariant: main-frame state cannot be assumed to cover workers
license_note: MIT

value_unit: mask overridden JavaScript functions as native
separability: standalone decision unit
decision_rationale: Native-looking function masking is an anti-detection/evasion mechanism and is outside LumiNet production authority.
invariant: privacy features remain explainable and do not forge native implementation provenance
negative_invariant: target code must not hide instrumentation by falsifying native-function appearance
license_note: MIT

separability: standalone decision unit
decision_rationale: Falsifying browser permission state would duplicate browser authority and can mislead callers.
invariant: browser permission truth remains browser-owned
negative_invariant: network tools must not forge user-agent permission state
license_note: MIT

value_unit: synchronize browser location presets with observed VPN region
separability: standalone decision unit
decision_rationale: Useful UX evidence that network exit and browser identity can drift and should be shown separately.
invariant: cross-layer identity state is explicit and reconciled rather than conflated
negative_invariant: a VPN region hint is not authoritative browser geolocation
license_note: MIT

separability: standalone decision unit
decision_rationale: Early bootstrap timing is relevant only to a browser-injection product and does not justify a LumiNet extension plane.
invariant: identity hooks require defined startup ordering if ever implemented
negative_invariant: late injection must not be claimed as complete page coverage
license_note: MIT

value_unit: Safari WebExtension native bridge and packaging boundary
separability: standalone decision unit
decision_rationale: Cross-browser packaging is product reference only; LumiNet release authority remains its existing desktop/mobile packages.
invariant: platform-specific browser packaging has explicit provenance
negative_invariant: peer Safari bundles do not become LumiNet release inputs
license_note: MIT

separability: standalone decision unit
decision_rationale: Explicit socket protection reinforces the existing LumiNet VpnService.protect bridge; no second VPN service is needed.
invariant: tunnel-originated sockets use one platform-owned VPN bypass boundary
negative_invariant: peer VpnService cannot become a second Android network authority
license_note: GPL-3.0 with additional terms; bundled components separately licensed

separability: standalone decision unit
decision_rationale: Per-app routing is useful product evidence, but LumiNet correctly reports it unsupported until packet/process routing can enforce it.
invariant: availability reflects enforcement capability, not UI presence
